commit_message:
[interpreter] Elide more TDZ hole checks

Add an analysis to the BytecodeGenerator that elides subsequent hole
checks after the first one in basic blocks.

Guarded by --ignition-elide-redundant-tdz-checks.

For more details, see
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1klT7-tQpxtYbwhssRDKfUMEgm-NS3iUeMuApuRgZnAw/edit?usp=sharing

diff --git a/test/unittests/interpreter/bytecode-generator-unittest.cc b/test/unittests/interpreter/bytecode-generator-unittest.cc
index eb855dd4d67..530294db7f4 100644
--- a/test/unittests/interpreter/bytecode-generator-unittest.cc
+++ b/test/unittests/interpreter/bytecode-generator-unittest.cc
@@ -3202,8 +3202,103 @@ TEST_F(BytecodeGeneratorTest, ElideRedundantLoadOperationOfImmutableContext) {
   CHECK(CompareTexts(
       BuildActual(printer(), snippets),
       LoadGolden("ElideRedundantLoadOperationOfImmutableContext.golden")));
 }
 
+TEST_F(BytecodeGeneratorTest, ElideRedundantHoleChecks) {
+  i::v8_flags.ignition_elide_redundant_tdz_checks = true;
+
+  printer().set_wrap(false);
+  printer().set_test_function_name("f");
+
+  // clang-format off
+  std::string snippets[] = {
+    // No control flow
+    "x; x;\n",
+
+    // 1-armed if
+    "if (x) { y; }\n"
+    "x + y;\n",
+
+    // 2-armed if
+    "if (a) { x; y; } else { x; z; }\n"
+    "x; y; z;\n",
+
+    // while
+    "while (x) { y; }\n"
+    "x; y;\n",
+
+    // do-while
+    "do { x; } while (y);\n"
+    "x; y;\n",
+
+    // C-style for
+    "for (x; y; z) { w; }\n"
+    "x; y; z; w;\n",
+
+    // for-in
+    "for (x in [y]) { z; }\n"
+    "x; y; z;\n",
+
+    // for-of
+    "for (x of [y]) { z; }\n"
+    "x; y; z;\n",
+
+    // try-catch
+    "try { x; } catch (y) { y; z; } finally { w; }\n"
+    "x; y; z; w;\n",
+
+    // destructuring init
+    "let { p = x } = { p: 42 }\n"
+    "x;\n",
+
+    // binary and
+    "let res = x && y && z\n"
+    "x; y; z;\n",
+
+    // binary or
+    "let res = x || y || z\n"
+    "x; y; z;\n",
+
+    // binary nullish
+    "let res = x ?? y ?? z\n"
+    "x; y; z;\n",
+
+    // optional chaining
+    "({p:42})?.[x]?.[x]?.[y];\n"
+    "x; y;\n",
+
+    // conditional and assignment
+    "x &&= y;\n"
+    "x; y;\n",
+
+    // conditional or assignment
+    "x ||= y;\n"
+    "x; y;\n",
+
+    // conditional nullish assignment
+    "x ??= y;\n"
+    "x; y;\n",
+
+    // switch
+    "switch (a) {\n"
+    "  case x: y; break;\n"
+    "  case 42: y; z;\n"
+    "  default: y; w;\n"
+    "}\n"
+    "x; y; z; w;\n"
+  };
+  // clang-format on
+
+  CHECK(CompareTexts(BuildActual(printer(), snippets,
+                                 "{\n"
+                                 "  f = function f(a) {\n",
+                                 "  }\n"
+                                 "  let w, x, y, z;\n"
+                                 "  f();\n"
+                                 "}\n"),
+                     LoadGolden("ElideRedundantHoleChecks.golden")));
+}
+
 }  // namespace interpreter
 }  // namespace internal
 }  // namespace v8

findings.title: TDZ hole checks incorrectly elided inside optional chain base expression
findings.message: In `BuildOptionalChain`, a `HoleCheckElisionScope elider(this)` was placed unconditionally before `expression_func()` is called. This caused all Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ) hole checks to be elided for any variable accessed as the BASE of an optional chain. When a TDZ variable (holding the internal sentinel TheHole) is the base of an optional chain, the expected `ThrowReferenceErrorIfHole` bytecode is not emitted. Because TheHole is not null/undefined, the subsequent `JumpIfUndefinedOrNull` optional chain check passes, allowing TheHole to propagate into JavaScript as if it were a real object. This bypasses the ECMAScript specification requirement that accessing an uninitialized binding throws a ReferenceError. The 'delete construct' variant specifically occurs when `delete tdz_var?.prop` is evaluated: the object load for `tdz_var` elides the hole check through the enclosing `BuildOptionalChain` hole check elision scope, allowing TheHole to leak. The fix moves `HoleCheckElisionScope` into `OptionalChainNullLabelScope` as a member, so it is correctly scoped and does not elide checks for the chain's base object loaded in outer contexts.
findings.suggestion: Move `HoleCheckElisionScope` from `BuildOptionalChain` into `OptionalChainNullLabelScope` as a member field initialized in the constructor. This restricts hole check elision to within the optional chain link scope (where dominance is guaranteed), rather than spanning the entire `BuildOptionalChain` call including its expression_func invocation. This prevents elision of hole checks for TDZ variables that serve as the base of an optional chain.

ground_truth.root_cause: The TDZ hole check elision optimization (`ignition_elide_redundant_tdz_checks`) added in `da0bcffa3d` placed `HoleCheckElisionScope elider(this)` at the start of `BuildOptionalChain`, covering the invocation of `expression_func()`. This function callback visits the actual chain expression, which may include TDZ variable accesses. The elision scope incorrectly treats all hole checks within the chain expression as redundant and suppresses them. The underlying assumption — that links 'earlier in the chain dominate later links' — applies to consecutive links of the same optional chain, but it incorrectly extends to the base object access itself, which is NOT dominated by any prior hole check.
